{"type":"text","timestamp":1794693612828,"sessionID":"ses_e23eec722ffeMD4srJK1cOThWq","part":{"id":"prt_1dc1340d2001t69RSw23C1cYVm","messageID":"msg_1dc131c9d001BxFguyGkDhL25t","sessionID":"ses_e23eec722ffeMD4srJK1cOThWq","type":"text","text":"The shift is over. All four customer-facing services have been at 0% errors since minute 68 and stayed there through minute 120. The early fixes were slow: mobile-api was failing 70–97% of requests until minute 66.\n\n**Causes and fixes**\n\n| Fault | Effect | Fix | Fixed at |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| promo-cache deploy v74 (minute −40) hardcoded the connection pool size to 4 | wishlist-svc failed ~4% of requests, so admin-portal and web-storefront each lost 4%. admin-portal earns $15,600/min, so this was the most expensive fault (~$620/min). | Scaled promo-cache from 4 to 8 replicas first, so retries during the rollback couldn't overload it. Then rolled back v74 and set it back to 4 replicas. | ~63 |\n| sitemap-svc config cfg-48 (minute −19) dropped `currency` from `price_fields` | sitemap-svc failed and a retry storm built on top, so partner-api failed ~77–86% | Throttled to 70% to stop the storm, then reverted cfg-48 and lifted the throttle | ~46 |\n| couriers-svc overloaded: its traffic is about 660 req/s but 3 replicas only handle about 315 | Retry storm, so mobile-api failed ~86% | Throttled to stop the storm and scaled to 9 replicas | 66 |\n| New fault at minute 45: profile-db config cfg-32 removed the `orders.write` token scope | risk-svc started failing, which kept couriers-svc and mobile-api down even after scaling | Reverted cfg-32 | 64 |\n\n**What cost extra**\n- **Early throttle lift:** I lifted the couriers-svc throttle at minute 16 before giving it more capacity. The retry storm came straight back, which cost about 20 more minutes of mobile-api failures.\n- **Replicas left above normal at the end:**\n  - **couriers-svc at 9 (normal 3):** it actually needs about 8, and I kept one spare.\n  - **reviews-svc at 11 (normal 8):** I scaled it at minute 76 as a precaution. It was at 98–99% CPU with traffic still rising, and a retry storm there would have reached admin-portal through inventory-svc and auth-svc.\n\n  Together that's about $27/min in replica charges.\n\nThe only mitigations that can count as wasted are rollbacks, config reverts, restarts and failovers. I used one rollback and two config reverts, each on the change that caused a fault, so there should be no wasted-mitigation charges.\n\nOther changes I reviewed but ruled out: wishlist-svc cfg-26, promo-cache cfg-55 and sitemap-svc v34.","time":{"start":1794693611730,"end":1794693612818}}}
